Clinical Supplies & Drugs — University H.description: Combined drugs and consumables spend at UHNM, inflated by cardiothoracic implants (valves, stents), trauma orthopaedic hardware and high-cost oncology SACT delivered at the Cancer Centre at Royal Stoke.
Clinical Supplies & Drugs — University H.beneficiaries: c.1.2m outpatient attendances and 165k admissions per year across Royal Stoke and County Hospital Stafford.
Clinical Supplies & Drugs — University H.legal_basis: NHS Act 2006; NHSE high-cost drugs pass-through reimbursement; NHS Group Accounting Manual 2024-25.
Clinical Supplies & Drugs — University H.notes: UHNM's clinical supply intensity (24% opex) is at the upper end of the major-trauma peer group due to high implant usage. Premises & Infrastructure — University H.beneficiaries: Users of two major hospital sites and 15 outpatient satellite locations.
Premises & Infrastructure — University H.legal_basis: NHS Act 2006; Project Company Agreement (PFI) 2007; NHS Group Accounting Manual 2024-25 IFRS-16.
Premises & Infrastructure — University H.notes: The Royal Stoke PFI is one of the NHS's largest outstanding unitary-charge obligations; expiry in 2044 will return the asset to the trust and remove c.GBP 50m of annual finance cost. Backlog maintenance at County Hospital remains a risk, with GBP 18m of high-risk estate flagged by 2024 ERIC return.
related: University Hospitals of North Midlands NHS Trust

Staff Costs — Guy's & St Thomas' NHS Fou.description: Payroll and temporary-workforce costs at Guy's & St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust (GSTT), a London tertiary/specialist provider running Guy's, St Thomas', Royal Brompton, Harefield and Evelina London children's hospitals. Staff costs are the single largest spend line, driven by consultant-heavy case-mix, specialist cardiothoracic and paediatric services, and Agenda-for-Change uplifts.
Staff Costs — Guy's & St Thomas' NHS Fou.beneficiaries: Circa 2.8M patient contacts per year across south-east London, SE England cardiothoracic network, and national paediatric tertiary referrals; ~24,000 substantive WTE.
Staff Costs — Guy's & St Thomas' NHS Fou.legal_basis: IFRS as adapted by DHSC Group Accounting Manual 2024-25; NHS Act 2006; Agenda for Change national terms.
Staff Costs — Guy's & St Thomas' NHS Fou.notes: GSTT is a London weighting / high-cost-area trust with structural pressure from consultant and specialist nursing recruitment. 2024-25 growth reflects the 5.5% AfC and 6% consultant award plus resident-doctor back-pay from the Oct 2024 BMA settlement. Agency spend is comparatively low for its scale reflecting a mature bank; NHSE off-framework ban bite was modest.

Clinical Supplies & Drugs — Guy's & St T.legal_basis: NHS Standard Contract; NHS England Commercial Medicines Unit framework; Specialised Services Commissioning (NHS Act 2006 s.3B).

Clinical Supplies & Drugs — Guy's & St T.notes: Growth is driven by high-cost drug volume (new CF modulators, advanced therapies, oncology biologics) plus tariff-excluded devices for cardiothoracic surgery. Most specialised drug cost is pass-through so net P&L risk is limited, but working-capital strain is material. NHS SBS and CMU framework compliance is strong.

Premises & Infrastructure — Guy's & St T.description: Estate running costs at GSTT including the two major PFI schemes — St Thomas' (Catalyst Healthcare, 2000) and Evelina London (Project PFI 2005) — plus Royal Brompton and Harefield sites. Unitary-charge uprating and energy inflation are the main cost drivers.
Premises & Infrastructure — Guy's & St T.beneficiaries: Operational occupants of 4 hospital sites (~530,000 sq m GIA); patients using specialist, tertiary and community facilities across central/south-east London.
Premises & Infrastructure — Guy's & St T.legal_basis: NHS (Residual Liabilities) Act 1996; PFI concession contracts under NHS Act 2006; ERIC return statutory duty.
Premises & Infrastructure — Guy's & St T.notes: GSTT carries one of the largest PFI unitary-charge burdens in the NHS and one of the highest ERIC backlogs (>£1B), a structural legacy of aged St Thomas' tower blocks. The St Thomas' PFI handback in 2031 is a major strategic risk — contract-expiry planning is under way with DHSC/NHSE PFI Centre of Excellence.

Drugs costs — The Clatterbridge Cancer C.notes: As a specialist cancer trust, virtually every pound of drug spend is oncology: checkpoint inhibitors, CDK4/6 inhibitors (palbociclib, abemaciclib, ribociclib), antibody-drug conjugates, and increasing oral targeted therapy volumes via the aseptic unit and homecare. The trust is a reference site for biosimilar adoption (trastuzumab, rituximab, bevacizumab in 2024). Notably, Cancer Drugs Fund spend is NOT in this line — it is centrally commissioned by NHS England (£340M national budget 2024-25) and passed to the trust at cost.
